record.original_question: Let sum_{i=0}^d h_i t^i be a polynomial with only real roots such that h_0 = 1 and h_0 < h_1 < ... < h_k for some 0 <= k <= d. Must there exist a simplicial complex whose f-vector is (h_0, h_1 - h_0, ..., h_k - h_{k-1})?

evidence.quote: Problem 2.10. Let sum_{i=0}^d h_i t^i in N[t] be a polynomial with only real roots such that h_0 = 1 and h_0 < h_1 < ... < h_k for some 0 <= k <= d. Is there a simplicial complex whose f-vector is (h_0, h_1 - h_0, ..., h_k - h_{k-1})?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $h(t)=\sum_{i=0}^{d}h_i t^i \in \mathbb{N}[t]$ be a polynomial with nonnegative integer coefficients all of whose roots are real. Suppose that $h_0=1$ and that for some integer $k$ with $0\le k\le d$ one has the strict inequalities
$$h_0<h_1<\cdots<h_k.$$
Define the vector
$$f=(h_0,\; h_1-h_0,\; h_2-h_1,\; \dots,\; h_k-h_{k-1}).$$
Must there exist a (finite abstract) simplicial complex $\Delta$ whose $f$-vector equals $f$? Equivalently, recalling that the $f$-vector of $\Delta$ is $(f_{-1},f_0,f_1,\dots,f_{k-1})$ where $f_{-1}=1$ (counting the empty face) and $f_i$ is the number of $i$-dimensional faces of $\Delta$, does there always exist such a $\Delta$ with $f_{-1}=h_0=1$ and $f_{i}=h_{i+1}-h_i$ for $0\le i\le k-1$?
